 An organic baby food company co-founded by actress Jennifer Garner has recalled one of its products, which was sold at major retailers nationwide, including in South Carolina.
 Once Upon a Farm issued a voluntary recall Oct. 30 of its Tractor Wheels soft-baked bars due to a potential choking hazard for toddlers, the California-based company said in a news release.
 “This decision was based on three consumer complaints,” the release read. “We acted out of an abundance of caution, in the best interest of our customers and our commitment to quality.”
 The recalled products specifically are the Apple, Sweet Potato and Spinach Tractor Wheels; Strawberry, Pumpkin and Beet Tractor Wheels; and Banana, Pumpkin and Cauliflower Tractor Wheels, according to the release.
 Also on Oct. 30, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration warned customers not to buy or serve Tractor Wheels.
 “When chewed, the product reportedly forms a dry, sticky mass that standard choking interventions — including back blows and the Heimlich maneuver — may fail to dislodge,” the agency said in a release.
 Toddlers between the ages of 18 months and 2-and-a-half years are particularly impacted by the choking hazard, both releases said.
 Once Upon a Farm, founded in 2015, went public in February at a $742 million valuation. Its stock fell 37 percent Nov. 2 after news of the recall circulated.
 The company, which sells food for “babies, toddlers and big kids,” according to its website, has products in more than 25,000 stores across the country. Once Upon a Farm products can be primarily found at Target, Walmart , Costco, Sam’s Club, and national and regional grocery stores like Publix, Harris Teeter and more.
